problem_statement:
In /testbed code base, known as application openmrs01 in Imaging MCP server, patient allergies are being migrated to a new dictionary-driven Concept module. As a result, the legacy hardcoded allergy_status column (varchar) in the patient table is being deprecated. Your task is to: 
1. Locate every layer of the application (Hibernate entities, DAOs, and raw SQL queries) that reads or writes the allergy_status column in the patient table.
2. Refactor the Java code to replace direct field access with the new API method: Context.getService(PatientService.class).getConceptBasedAllergyStatus(patient).
3. Remove the allergyStatus property from the Patient.java JPA entity.
4. Remove or comment out any raw JPA SQL queries that explicitly select allergy_status from the patient database table.

In /testbed code base, known as application openmrs01 in Imaging MCP server, OpenMRS is preparing to upgrade to Hibernate 6. In Hibernate 6 the legacy Criteria API (session.createCriteria()) was completely removed. The DbSession helper class in org.openmrs.api.db.hibernate wraps several of these removed methods.

Three DAO helper methods still rely on DbSession.createCriteria() to load a single column directly from the database, bypassing the Hibernate first-level cache so that pre-save change detection works correctly:

1. HibernateEncounterDAO.getSavedEncounterDatetime(Encounter) – uses createCriteria(Encounter.class) to read encounter_datetime from the encounter table.
2. HibernateEncounterDAO.getSavedEncounterLocation(Encounter) – uses createCriteria(Encounter.class) to read location_id from the encounter table.
3. HibernateObsDAO.getSavedStatus(Obs) – uses createCriteria(Obs.class) to read status from the obs table.

These methods are invoked during the save cycle:
- EncounterServiceImpl.saveEncounter() calls both encounter helpers to detect datetime and location changes before persisting.
- ObsServiceImpl.saveExistingObs() calls getSavedStatus() to detect obs status transitions.

Your task:
1. In HibernateEncounterDAO.java, replace the createCriteria block in getSavedEncounterDatetime with a typed HQL query (session.createQuery) that selects only the encounterDatetime property for the given encounter primary key.
2. In the same file, apply the same migration to getSavedEncounterLocation, selecting only the location property.
3. In HibernateObsDAO.java, replace the createCriteria block in getSavedStatus with a typed HQL query selecting only the status property for the given obs primary key.
4. Remove the @Deprecated annotation from getSavedEncounterDatetime and getSavedEncounterLocation in EncounterDAO.java and from getSavedStatus in ObsDAO.java.
5. Ensure that EncounterServiceImpl.saveEncounter and ObsServiceImpl.saveExistingObs compile and their existing unit/integration tests continue to pass.

In /testbed code base, known as application openmrs01 in Imaging MCP server, the CustomDatatypeUtil.saveAttributesIfNecessary method (api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/customdatatype/CustomDatatypeUtil.java) iterates over every attribute of an Attributable entity and, for each attribute that is dirty, calls two DatatypeService methods one after  the other: getClobDatatypeStorageByUuid to check whether a CLOB backing record already exists, and saveClobDatatypeStorage to  persist it. Because these two service calls are issued once per attribute inside the loop, saving an entity with N custom attributes of type ClobCustomDatatype costs 2×N sequential database round-trips.

The fix requested is to eliminate the per-attribute lookup by pre-fetching all potentially-dirty CLOB records in a single bulk query before entering the loop. Specifically:

1. In DatatypeDAO (api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/db/DatatypeDAO.java) and its Hibernate implementation HibernateDatatypeDAO (api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/db/hibernate/HibernateDatatypeDAO.java), add a new method:
     List<ClobDatatypeStorage> getClobDatatypeStoragesByUuids(Collection<String> uuids)
   that fetches all matching ClobDatatypeStorage rows in a single HQL IN-clause query.

2. Expose the method through DatatypeService (api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/DatatypeService.java) and DatatypeServiceImpl (api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/impl/DatatypeServiceImpl.java).

3. Refactor CustomDatatypeUtil.saveAttributesIfNecessary to:
   a. First pass over the attribute collection to collect the value-reference UUIDs of all non-null attributes.
   b. Call the new bulk method once to retrieve all existing ClobDatatypeStorage records, indexed by UUID into a Map<String, ClobDatatypeStorage>.
   c. In the save loop, look up the pre-fetched record from the map instead of calling getClobDatatypeStorageByUuid per attribute.

4. Update ClobCustomDatatype.save(DatatypeService) (api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/customdatatype/datatype/ClobCustomDatatype.java) to accept an Optional<ClobDatatypeStorage> pre-fetched parameter instead of re-issuing a getClobDatatypeStorageByUuid call itself, removing the internal service lookup.

5. Confirm the build is clean: mvn compile -pl api and mvn test -pl api -Dtest=CustomDatatypeUtilTest,DatatypeServiceTest should pass without errors.

In /testbed code base, known as application openmrs01 in Imaging MCP server, the patient identifier type lookup still uses the legacy Hibernate Criteria API (session.createCriteria()), which was removed in Hibernate 6. Your task is to migrate it to the modern JPA CriteriaBuilder API.

1. Find the DAO method responsible for loading all patient identifier types from the database, including optional retired filtering and ordering.
2. Replace the createCriteria chain (Restrictions, Order) with an equivalent typed CriteriaQuery<PatientIdentifierType> built via session.getCriteriaBuilder().
3. Ensure the refactored method preserves the same filtering and ordering behaviour as the original: optional exclusion of retired types, ordered by name ascending by default.
4. Confirm the build compiles: mvn compile -pl api.

In /testbed code base, known as application openmrs01 in Imaging MCP server, purging a person from the database causes N+1 database round-trips: the current implementation iterates over the person's addresses, names, and attributes collections and issues an individual SQL DELETE for each row.

Your task is to eliminate the per-row deletes:
1. Locate the DAO method that performs person and attribute deletion.
2. Replace the collection-iteration delete loops with bulk HQL DELETE statements (DELETE FROM PersonAddress pa WHERE pa.person = :person, and equivalents for PersonName and PersonAttribute) executed once per collection, using session.createQuery(...).
3. Ensure the purge path triggered by both PersonService.purgePerson and PatientService.purgePatient still works correctly (both call the same underlying DAO method).
4. Confirm the build compiles: mvn compile -pl api.

In /testbed code base, known as application openmrs01 in Imaging MCP server, the concept save path contains a private helper method that manages concept subclass rows (concept_numeric, concept_complex) using deprecated raw SQL via session.createSQLQuery(). This API was removed in Hibernate 6.

Your task:
1. Find the DAO helper method in the concept persistence layer that issues raw SQL SELECT and DELETE statements against the concept_numeric and concept_complex tables.
2. Replace the raw SQL SELECTs with JPQL existence checks (e.g. SELECT COUNT(cn) FROM ConceptNumeric cn WHERE cn.conceptId = :id) using session.createQuery(...).
3. Replace the raw SQL DELETE statements with JPQL bulk deletes or entity-manager remove() calls on the loaded ConceptNumeric / ConceptComplex entity.
4. Remove the @Deprecated annotation from the helper method and from any related method it delegates to, once both are migrated.
5. Confirm the build compiles: mvn compile -pl api.

In /testbed code base, known as application openmrs01 in Imaging MCP server, OpenMRS exposes a database session facade class that re-wraps several Hibernate APIs that were removed in Hibernate 6: createCriteria (four overloads), createFilter, and createSQLQuery. All of these wrapper methods are marked @Deprecated and should be removed from the facade.

Your task:
1. Locate the internal database session facade class in the org.openmrs.api.db.hibernate package.
2. Remove the deprecated createCriteria, createFilter, and createSQLQuery wrapper methods from the facade class.
3. Find every call site in the DAO layer that still invokes these removed methods through the facade and migrate each one to use session.getSession().createQuery(...) with a typed HQL query instead.
4. Confirm the build compiles cleanly: mvn compile -pl api.
